title: Do Deterministic Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs Under a Shared-Candidate Budget?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates the practical question: given a single hosted-model generation per intent, does a deterministic generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard applied to the same candidate improve emulator-executable success? Generation requested gpt-5-mini; the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤ 1 (no extra LLM calls). Primary outcomes (artifact-backed): baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We incorporate two artifact-grounded clarifications: (1) aggregated difficulty-label counts across the 200 confirmatory intents (easy=20, medium=80, hard=60, very_hard=40), and (2) a concise auditable exemplar of the single repaired episode (task_id task-000137: validator_violation MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND; deterministic repair = canonical insertion of the missing required command at the manifest position; validation_before.valid == false → validation_after.valid == true). All run traces, prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) changes with large language models (LLMs) promises reduced manual effort but raises an operational-safety question: do LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Prior work demonstrates intent-to-configuration prototypes and documents structured-output failures (e.g., missing required commands, misordering, or protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool-augmentation. Despite these proposals, execution-grounded evidence that quantifies the marginal benefit of applying a bounded deterministic repair to the same initial LLM candidate under a constrained hosted-call budget remains limited.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates the “repair-on-same-candidate” question by sharing a single initial LLM candidate across both arms (baseline ungated acceptance and guarded generate–verify–repair). The shared-candidate estimand answers a deployment-relevant question for operators constrained by per-call cost or governance limits: given one initial model output, does an auditable deterministic validator plus a single deterministic repair (when unambiguous) increase the proportion of emulator-executable configurations? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions and operational constraints of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; (3) complete execution accounting and exact-test justification appropriate for small-discordant-pair inference, including the preregistered bootstrap parameters; and (4) two artifact-grounded clarifications requested during review: the confirmatory-bank difficulty-label distribution and an auditable exemplar of the single deterministic repair that changed outcome.
sections.related_work: Three strands of literature motivate our study. First, intent-to-configuration work demonstrates that LLMs can map natural-language intents to vendor-like CLI sequences but documents structural and semantic errors that threaten execution safety; empirical prototype evaluations report promising translation accuracy in curated settings while highlighting missing commands, order errors, and unsafe modifications as key failure modes (Nguyen et al., 2024). Second, mitigation strategies from NetOps and adjacent structured-output domains include retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), live schema grounding (SAL), grammar- or constraint-aware decoding, and verifier-assisted repair; these approaches reduce hallucination and format errors in domains such as NL2SQL and document-grounded generation but require careful domain adaptation for vendor CLI dialects and workflow policies (Mishra et al.; SAL; constrained-decoding literature). Third, deterministic verifiers and emulator-backed validators provide an assurance layer: formal-methods tools (NetKAT variants, weighted NetKAT, ensemble verifiers) check reachability and structural properties, and emulator-based checks detect many semantic violations before deployment. These verifiers have fidelity limits—dynamic control-plane timing, convergence, and vendor runtime idiosyncrasies are imperfectly modeled. Our study connects these strands by empirically measuring, under a constrained-call practical estimand, the marginal yield of a conservative, deterministic GVR guard applied to the same initial LLM candidate.
sections.methodology:
We preregistered a paired, shared-initial-generation confirmatory protocol (preregistration cnd-001-5f3a). For each of n=200 curated natural-language intents the hosted model produced one initial candidate configuration (requested model gpt-5-mini). That shared candidate was scored as the baseline and also passed (unchanged) to the guarded arm. The guarded arm deterministically validated the candidate with a three-stage validator; if and only if the validator emitted a repairable, unambiguous violation the deterministic repair operator applied a single deterministic transformation (repair_budget ≤ 1 for the confirmatory run). No additional LLM calls were permitted for repairs; the single deterministic repair invocation in the run was executed by code. Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared initial generations + 1 deterministic repair invocation recorded in provider-stage accounting).

Task bank and scoring: The confirmatory bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs produced by a deterministic generator. Each task payload encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (authoritative ordered commands), workflow policies (make-before-break, protected-interface constraints), and difficulty metadata. The scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) requires: (a) syntactic parse into canonical CLI-like statements; (b) inclusion of the task’s required_sequence with correct presence/order; (c) respect for dependency and group-activity policies; (d) preservation of protected-interface values; and (e) exact equality between emulator-observed final_state and expected_final_state. Provider/API generation failures are treated per the preregistered missingness plan as arm failures; none occurred in this confirmatory run.

Deterministic validator and repair operator: The validator executes three ordered deterministic stages and emits a machine-readable trace. Stage 1: syntactic parsing and canonical normalization; Stage 2: structural/workflow checks emitting violation codes (e.g., MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION); Stage 3: deterministic application in a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator and exact final_state comparison. The repair operator is a deterministic rule-based transformer applied only when violation_count>0 and the violation family is in a preregistered repairable set and the repair mapping is unambiguous. Canonical transformations include inserting missing required commands at manifest-specified canonical positions, stable reordering of annotated blocks, and enforcement of protected fields; abstention occurs when multiple equally plausible deterministic repairs exist. All validator traces, repair decisions, and before/after normalized configurations were recorded for audit.

Analysis plan and statistical reasoning: The preregistered primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline). The primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar (implemented as the two-sided binomial on discordant pairs), appropriate for small discordant counts; we complemented this with a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) to bound plausible paired differences. The preregistered absolute-effect target for power planning was 0.15, but that target assumed a non-near-ceiling baseline; the realized baseline substantially exceeded those planning assumptions, constraining inferential sensitivity.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 paired intents) without provider/API failures. Condition-level counts: baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995); guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency table is n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and interval estimates: With observed discordant total n = n10 + n01 = 1 and k = n10 = 1, the preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (two-sided binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) gives a 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]. Under these data the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the baseline was near-ceiling, reducing possible discordant counts.

Repair and failure diagnostics: Validator traces reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1; that single deterministic repair converted the episode into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10=1). Syntactic/parse failures = 0. Provider-call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1.

Difficulty distribution (reviewer clarification): The confirmatory bank difficulty-label counts are: easy = 20, medium = 80, hard = 60, very_hard = 40 (sum = 200). This stratification informed task selection and documents that the confirmatory set intentionally emphasized medium-to-very-hard cases.

Auditable exemplar (reviewer clarification): The single repaired episode that produced the guarded-only success is recorded in the archived manifest as task_id task-000137. In that episode the validator reported validation_before.violation_codes = ["MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND"] and violation_count = 1. The deterministic repair operator applied the canonical Insertion transformation (inserting the missing required command at the canonical position derived from required_sequence). After the deterministic insertion the validator observed validation_after.valid == true; the post-repair normalized configuration passed the full intent constraint checks. All before/after normalized configurations and the repair trace are archived for audit.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution, ungated gpt-5-mini generation produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic validators provide structured violation codes that enable targeted deterministic repairs; in this low-error regime the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, the guarded shared-candidate design preserves low hosted-call cost while providing an assurance gate whose principal value is auditability and clear failure-mode logging rather than large marginal increases in pass rate.

Sensitivity and statistical considerations: The exact McNemar is the appropriate small-sample paired test here; the chi-squared approximation is invalid for small discordant counts. The paired-bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) complements the exact test by showing the plausible range of paired differences consistent with the observed pairs. Near-ceiling baselines limit sensitivity to detect moderate absolute improvements: with 200 pairs and a baseline ≈0.995, only very small absolute headroom exists for improvement unless the task distribution includes substantially more challenging or adversarial intents.

Design-space trade-offs and practitioner guidance: Shared-candidate guarded designs are recommended where hosted-call budgets, strict auditability, and deterministic accountability dominate decision-making. If maximizing pass rates is the primary objective and additional provider cost is acceptable, independent-resampling (multiple LLM draws per intent) or LLM-invoked repair loops will likely increase yield but incur higher costs and governance complexity. Deterministic validators should be treated as mandatory assurance machinery where auditable, repeatable checks and low-latency failure explanations are required.

Threats to validity and limitations: Internal validity is strong for the paired estimand because both arms evaluate the same initial candidate. Construct validity depends on emulator fidelity: the deterministic emulator models control-plane state but cannot fully capture runtime effects such as BGP convergence delays or vendor firmware idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by the single evaluated model (gpt-5-mini) and the synthetic curated bank focused on small changes; extrapolation to broader multivendor CLI diversity or adversarial intents is limited. Conclusion validity is constrained by the near-ceiling baseline that reduced discordant-pair counts; larger or differently distributed task banks would be required to assess substantial absolute improvements of guarded designs under this estimand.

Reproducibility and auditability: All artifacts needed to reproduce analysis and inspection are archived in the study evidence bundle, including per-episode prompts/responses, provider-call traces, validator traces, the single deterministic repair trace, analysis scripts, contingency tables, and bootstrap parameters. The preregistered analysis procedures (exact McNemar on discordant pairs; paired-bootstrap with 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) were executed as specified and produced the reported p-value and CI. Execution accounting: completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 201.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment that measured whether a bounded deterministic generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and curated task distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded negligible marginal improvement; deterministic validators, however, remain valuable auditable assurance gates for operational NetOps pipelines. The archived evidence bundle contains run traces and artifacts for independent audit and reanalysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: Generation requested gpt-5-mini. Validation used a deterministic netops validator implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by the study adapter. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤ 1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting: the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage invocations = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.
Full per-task difficulty labels and all run traces are archived in the study evidence bundle for audit and per-task inspection.
